title: Alloparental Care Protocol
author: Andrea Vogel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j6pcrdn

steps.title: Prepare animal, cage, and recording setup
steps.instruction: Gather all required materials and configure the testing arena before any behavioral observation.

substeps.instruction: Obtain experimental animals that are at least 8 weeks old and breeder cages.
Confirm that the pups to be used are 2–6 days old.
Retrieve a rat cage; if it contains bedding, remove the paper, otherwise add just enough bedding to cover the bottom.
Set up the tripod and camera, adjusting position until the whole cage is visible in the frame.
Place a colored notecard displaying the experimental animal’s ear‑tag number beside the cage, ensuring the number is visible on camera.
Record the experimental animal’s information on the behavior worksheet.

steps.title: Place pups and start recording
steps.instruction: Introduce the pups and the experimental animal into the arena and begin video capture.

substeps.instruction: Choose a breeder cage and obtain two pups (use a single pup when testing experimental females).
Record the breeder cage number and the age of the pups on the worksheet.
Place the pups in one of the two corners farthest from the camera.
Press the record button on the camera.
Place the experimental animal on the opposite side of the cage from the pups.
Start a timer for 5.5 minutes and record the start time.

steps.title: Observe for 5.5 minutes and stop
steps.instruction: Conduct the observation period and end the recording, noting any aggression.

substeps.instruction: After 5.5 minutes, stop recording and record the stop time.
If aggression occurs, stop recording immediately and remove the pups.

steps.title: Post-test handling and cage cleaning
steps.instruction: Process the animal after the test, clean the arena, and prepare for the next trial.

substeps.instruction: Hand the experimental animal to the person running the Resident Intruder test.
Each pair of pups is used twice; for experimental females, test one pup at a time.
Wipe the sides of the cage with 70 % ethanol between the first and second use of the pups.
After the second use, empty the cage, wipe the sides again with 70 % ethanol, add fresh bedding, and place a new ear‑tag notecard beside the cage.
Repeat the entire procedure for the next experimental animal.
